Standard: Crewmembers in air vehicles that can exceed 4.5g require physiological protection during high-g maneuvers. G protection may include but is not limited to the following: lower body coverage (anti-g suit or trousers), g sensing valve (to inflate the suit), PBG breathing regulator, optional upper body coverage, and occipital bladder on the helmet. G protection provisions are compatible with AFE, and pressures are IAW FIGURE 1 and FIGURE 2. If upper counterpressure garment is used, it is to inflate prior to the lower pressure garment. Inflations will be properly coupled with the ACBS. FIGURE 1. G-suit pressure schedule. FIGURE 2. PBG pressure schedule. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
(1) Lab test: G system pressure regulation - Test the g protection system in an unmanned state to verify pressure regulation capability IAW FIGURE 1 and FIGURE 2. This testing will verify that over pressurization of the system cannot occur.
(2) Lab test: Conduct qualification testing in a centrifuge environment. Test the system first unmanned to verify system performance, followed by manned testing to assess functional operation and crewmember tolerance and endurance, and that the system complies with FIGURE 1 and FIGURE 2. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
(3) Flight test: Conduct a flight test program to assess relevant environmental and operational conditions. Results of the flight test data will be evaluated to confirm conformance to the g pressure schedule and PBG schedule as applicable.
